### Passing integration: SpaceBattles Fic Search Thread

The first-party thread at `https://forums.spacebattles.com/threads/fic-search-thread.134658/` is specifically for stories/fics that a reader knows existed and previously encountered but can no longer find; current visible guidance distinguishes this task from general recommendations. SpaceBattles' first-party terms state that users retain copyright over their submitted content while granting the service the license needed to operate and publish it.

WebNR therefore admits only a WebNR-authored local-YAML catalog row containing the stable first-party URL, task description, tags, date, region, and `Link-only-WebNR-editorial` marker. No forum post, username, reply, vote/reaction, story text, rating, account state, attachment, crawler, API client, login, cookie, CAPTCHA bypass, or background request is copied or introduced. Readers navigate to SpaceBattles under SpaceBattles' own controls.

The new row is distinct from the existing broad SpaceBattles Story Ideas & Recommendations route: this one recovers a **specific fic known to have existed**, analogous to Royal Road's separate forgotten-title task but for a different platform/community. `Web Novel Discussion Radar Starter` therefore increases from 11 to **12 link-only rows** while the maintained source-family count remains **26**.

### Fully audited deferrals

- **SFF Stack Exchange `story-identification`:** first-party guidance explicitly covers identifying a unique science-fiction/fantasy work, including websites and fanfic, and asks for medium, approximate date, plot, setting, characters, language, and ruled-out candidates. It is cited in the reader guide but not admitted as a maintained Radar row today because its remit also covers film, television, games, comics, and other media.
- **LibraryThing `Name that Book`:** the public group is purpose-built for finding a forgotten book title, but current LibraryThing terms distinguish ordinary human use from unauthorized automated/systematic collection and headless/AI-agent access. WebNR therefore keeps it as a manual reader route only and does not make it a source-synchronization or automated health dependency.
